customManagers.description: Upstream versions of the bundled MCP servers, pinned as a git ref in bundled/<name>/server.yaml. Renovate reads package.json and nothing else by default, so these were invisible and drifted a long way: chrome-devtools-mcp sat at 0.12.1 against an upstream 1.9.0, and browser-tools-mcp at v1.2.0 against v2.0.2. chrome-devtools is the second largest tool group shipped, so a stale pin there is not cosmetic.

Versions of the local MCP servers launched through npx, pinned inline in the launch string rather than declared as dependencies. @playwright/mcp was pinned at 0.0.52 against an upstream 0.0.80, and @mobilenext/mobile-mcp at 0.0.33 against 1.0.4.

packageRules.description: chrome-devtools-mcp tags carry the package name as a prefix, as in chrome-devtools-mcp-v1.9.0, so the version has to be extracted before it can be compared. Without this the tags sort as plain strings and the newest release is not recognised.

Bundled MCP servers ship inside the released binary, and a major bump can rename or re-shape the tools a client sees. Separate PRs per package keep each one reviewable, since adopting one means re-verifying its tools against a real target.

markdown2pdf-mcp is pinned to the commit 687dbfa rather than a tag, and a commit cannot be compared against a tag list, so Renovate would either skip it or report nonsense. Upstream does publish tags and is currently at v2.1.3. Left disabled deliberately: moving from a commit to a tag changes what is bundled and should be a considered switch, not an automated bump.
